about: The models corpus_bench.py measures, smallest first, each with one edit whose `from` occurs exactly once in its file. `root` is relative to the repository (`tom`'s is the checkout beside it, in its own repository); `cwd`, `pythonpath`, `xbf`, `needs` and the edit's `file` are relative to the model's root; `targets` and the script in `document` to its `cwd`; `document` selects a built report as script.py::function, and `xbf` is a separate explicit export.

models.name: l_bracket
models.note: the small example: one filleted part

models.name: planetary_gear
models.note: the docs hero, whose GLB apps/docs/scripts/sync-hero-glb.mjs exports

models.name: juno
models.note: Runs juno.py, including its 28 explicit link-model calls, then selects the juno assembly document.
models.comparison_note: The recorded old Juno build measured the robot alone; this script also builds its 28 link documents. Build speedups are not comparable.

models.name: tom
models.note: the arm lives in its own repository, the checkout beside this one (a worktree has no sibling: give --config a copy of this file with the way up); builds from its root with src on PYTHONPATH and reads its pinned STEP/imported (Git LFS)

models.name: hypercar
models.note: the old benchmark's edit, LOWER_ARM's first point 22 -> 23 (src/README.md); since the corpus migration a plain @model that declares no GLB (its clips ride the document)
